rationale: Both named blockers are materially fixed: stopEpoch is a 0..2^53-1 SQLite INTEGER with a typeof/bounds CHECK, app-computed safe-integer update in one IMMEDIATE transaction and fail-closed STOP_EPOCH_EXHAUSTED (no BigInt, no old+1, no wraparound); and authorization is exact-UID SO_PEERCRED matching against a root-owned, O_NOFOLLOW/ownership/mode-validated role allowlist with groups explicitly non-authorizing and no model UID path. checkAndConsume remains privileged dormant state with no V1C production consumer or route. Residual caveat: binding grant validity to equality with the current global stopEpoch means any increment mass-invalidates all outstanding grants — acceptable as fail-closed, but the operational intent should be documented at implementation.
